title: Installing and using uv: a follow-along session

citations.claim: Standalone installer, the install command for this session
A new shell is required after the installer edits shell profiles
citations.verbatim: Then restart the shell or source the shell config file.

citations.claim: Uninstall path, and the pre-0.5.0 ~/.cargo/bin gotcha

environment_of_record.note: The cited documentation references uv 0.12.19. This machine runs 0.12.2, seventeen patch versions behind, so every expected_output in this storyboard is a PATTERN and never a literal version string.

chapters.title: Install uv and prove it works
chapters.start_state: A Linux or macOS shell. `uv` is NOT installed. `curl` is present. Network access is available.

steps.purpose: Install uv from Astral's standalone installer.
steps.precondition: Network available; `curl` present; on macOS or Linux.
steps.checkpoint: The installer names the directory it installed into.
steps.state_change: Creates ~/.local/bin/uv and ~/.local/bin/uvx; appends a PATH line to the shell profile.
steps.common_failure: If `curl` is absent the command fails with `curl: command not found`; use the `wget -qO- ... | sh` form from the same page.
steps.replay_skip_reason: Installs software and rewrites the shell profile. Verified by citation and by the measured install location, not by re-execution. This step is the one place where re-running is not merely expensive but changes the machine under the test.

steps.purpose: Show the trap: this shell still cannot find uv.
steps.precondition: The install step has run. The CURRENT shell was open before the install.
steps.checkpoint: You see `not found` even though the install succeeded. This is expected.
steps.state_change: None. Nothing is installed or removed by this step.
steps.common_failure: Learners read this as a failed install. It is not -- the binary is on disk; the open shell has not re-read the profile.

steps.purpose: Open a new shell and prove the install worked.
steps.checkpoint: The path printed ends in `/uv` and is under your home directory.
steps.state_change: A login shell reads ~/.profile, which is where the installer added ~/.local/bin to PATH.
steps.common_failure: If this still prints nothing, the installer did not edit your profile. Re-run with the version-pinned URL from the same documentation page.

steps.purpose: Record the version every later expectation is written against.
steps.checkpoint: You have a three-part version number written down.
steps.common_failure: A version below 0.5.0 installed into ~/.cargo/bin, so `which uv` may point there. See the uninstall note on the cited page.

chapters.title: Create a first project
chapters.start_state: `uv` on PATH. A directory you can write to. No project exists here yet.
chapters.goal: A project directory with a `pyproject.toml` you did not have to write by hand.

steps.purpose: Choose where the project lives, and say it out loud on screen.
steps.checkpoint: The printed path ENDS IN `uv-demo`. This is the step that stops directory drift later.
steps.state_change: Creates the working directory uv-demo and makes it the current directory.
steps.common_failure: If the path does not end in uv-demo, you are somewhere else and every later relative path will be wrong.

steps.precondition: Current directory is the uv-demo directory created by make-project-dir.
steps.checkpoint: Three things exist: pyproject.toml, README.md, src.
steps.state_change: Creates pyproject.toml, README.md and src/ in the current directory.
steps.common_failure: If uv is not on PATH this fails with `uv: not found` -- go back to chapter 1.

steps.purpose: Show the one line that everything later depends on.
steps.checkpoint: You can read the Python constraint aloud. It is a constraint, not a comment.
steps.common_failure: A constraint like >=3.99 that names no real interpreter makes every later command fail; see the negative scene in chapter 5.

chapters.title: Add a dependency to the project
chapters.start_state: A uv-demo project with an empty dependencies list.
chapters.goal: A recorded requirement, and a resolved lockfile.

steps.purpose: Add a dependency, and let the tool record it.
steps.precondition: Current directory is the uv-demo project root, where pyproject.toml exists.
steps.checkpoint: You see `requests==` with an EXACT pin, not a range, and you see the other packages it pulled in.
steps.state_change: Appends the requirement to pyproject.toml and writes uv.lock.
steps.common_failure: Running this outside the project root writes a new project instead of editing the existing one.

steps.purpose: Prove the dependency is a project fact and not just an environment fact.
steps.checkpoint: The dependency is visible in the file, not only in the terminal output.
steps.common_failure: If the file does not list it, the command ran somewhere else.

chapters.title: Lock and sync: two different jobs
chapters.start_state: A project with one recorded dependency and a lockfile.
chapters.goal: A lockfile you can review, and an environment that matches it.

steps.purpose: Resolve the graph and write down the answer, without installing anything.
steps.checkpoint: A resolution count appears AND you notice no packages were installed.
steps.state_change: Writes uv.lock. Installs nothing. This distinction is the whole point of the step.
steps.common_failure: Treating lock as install; then you have no way to review a resolution before adopting it.

steps.purpose: Prove the answer was written to a file you can commit.
steps.common_failure: If this fails, lock did not run in this directory.

chapters.title: Run code, and borrow a package for one command
chapters.start_state: A locked project. The interpreter constraint has not yet been observed in action.
chapters.goal: Code running in a project-local environment, and one throwaway dependency that is deliberately not recorded.

steps.purpose: Create the file the next step runs. Shown on screen, because an unshown file is an unshown-state dependency.
steps.precondition: Current directory is the uv-demo project root.
steps.checkpoint: src/main.py now exists. This is the step that closed the `shown versus created` gap.
steps.common_failure: If src/ does not already exist, mkdir -p creates it; without the -p the command fails when src is absent.

steps.purpose: See the project constraint enforced as an interpreter choice.
steps.precondition: create-main has run. A network fetch of a managed interpreter may occur on a clean machine.
steps.checkpoint: The printed version is a 3.12.x, NOT necessarily the system python3. That difference is the lesson.
steps.state_change: Creates .venv/ in the project. May download a managed interpreter on a clean machine -- measured 111 MB on this one, already cached since 2026-08-13, so this run fetched nothing.
steps.common_failure: ModuleNotFoundError means you ran before `uv add`; see the negative scene at the end of this chapter.

steps.purpose: Borrow a package for exactly one command, and prove it was not recorded.
steps.command: uv run --with rich python -c "import rich; print('borrowed')"
steps.checkpoint: The word `borrowed` prints, which means the import worked.
steps.state_change: Installs rich into a temporary environment. Writes NOTHING to pyproject.toml or uv.lock.
steps.common_failure: Using --with for a dependency the project actually needs; it will be missing on the next machine and nobody will know why.

steps.purpose: Prove the throwaway really was not recorded.
steps.common_failure: A non-zero count means the package was recorded, so it was added the wrong way.
